concepts.title: What HCI Studies: Users, Tasks, and Context
concepts.summary: HCI as a discipline: users, tasks, and context of use, why the interface is the system from the user's point of view, and how this differs from visual design alone.

concepts.title: Human Perception and Cognition for Interface Design
concepts.summary: Attention, memory limits, and Gestalt grouping, and what they imply for layout, feedback, and how much an interface may ask a person to remember.

concepts.title: Mental Models and the Gulfs of Execution and Evaluation
concepts.summary: Mental models and Norman's gulfs of execution and evaluation, with affordances, signifiers, mapping, and feedback as the tools that close them.

concepts.title: Fitts's Law and Hick's Law
concepts.summary: Two predictive models: Fitts's law for pointing time and Hick's law for choice time, with worked calculations on real target sizes and menus, and where each one stops applying.

concepts.title: Usability and Its Definition (ISO 9241-11)
concepts.summary: The ISO 9241-11 definition of usability: effectiveness, efficiency, and satisfaction for specified users, goals, and context, and how that makes usability measurable.

concepts.title: Nielsen's Ten Heuristics and Heuristic Evaluation
concepts.summary: Nielsen's ten heuristics and how to run a heuristic evaluation, including severity ratings and how many evaluators it takes.

concepts.title: Usability Testing and the System Usability Scale
concepts.summary: Planning a usability test, think-aloud, task success and time, and scoring the System Usability Scale correctly.

concepts.title: User Research: Interviews, Personas, Task Analysis
concepts.summary: Interviews and contextual inquiry, personas grounded in evidence instead of invention, and hierarchical task analysis.

concepts.title: Prototyping Fidelity: Sketch, Wireframe, Mockup, Prototype
concepts.summary: Sketch, wireframe, mockup, and prototype: the question each fidelity answers and the cost of testing at the wrong one.

concepts.title: Navigation, Menus, Windows, and Information Architecture
concepts.summary: Navigation patterns, menus, windows and dialogs, and the information architecture methods behind them, such as card sorting and tree testing.

concepts.title: Forms and Input Design
concepts.summary: Labels, input types, defaults, validation timing, and error messages, for forms people actually finish.

concepts.title: Color, Typography, and Icons
concepts.summary: Color contrast and color vision, typographic hierarchy and legibility, and when an icon needs a label.

concepts.title: Semiotic Engineering: Communicability and the Designer's Message
concepts.summary: Semiotic engineering: the interface as a message from designer to user, and the communicability evaluation method with its breakdown tags.

concepts.title: Accessibility and WCAG
concepts.summary: WCAG's four principles and conformance levels, semantic markup, keyboard access, and testing with assistive technology, against the current published version of the standard.

concepts.title: Internationalization and Localization
concepts.summary: Internationalization versus localization, text expansion, right-to-left layout, and date, number, and plural rules through Unicode CLDR and ICU.

concepts.title: Ubiquitous Computing and Post-WIMP Interaction
concepts.summary: Weiser's vision of ubiquitous computing and post-WIMP interaction through touch, voice, gesture, and context awareness, with what held up and what did not.

concepts.title: Visual Encoding and Perception in Data Visualization
concepts.summary: Cleveland and McGill's ranking of perceptual encodings, preattentive features, and choosing a chart by the comparison it has to support.

concepts.title: Capstone: Evaluating a Real Interface End to End
concepts.summary: One real interface evaluated across the whole discipline: task analysis, heuristic evaluation, a small usability test scored with SUS, a WCAG check, and a prioritized list of findings.
